ESV.1: “The whole commandment that I command you today you shall be careful to do, that you may live and multiply, and go in and possess the land that the LORD swore to give to your fathers.
ESV.2: And you shall remember the whole way that the LORD your God has led you these forty years in the wilderness, that he might humble you, testing you to know what was in your heart, whether you would keep his commandments or not.
ESV.3: And he humbled you and let you hunger and fed you with manna, which you did not know, nor did your fathers know, that he might make you know that man does not live by bread alone, but man lives by every word  that comes from the mouth of the LORD.
ESV.4: Your clothing did not wear out on you and your foot did not swell these forty years.
ESV.5: Know then in your heart that, as a man disciplines his son, the LORD your God disciplines you.
ESV.6: So you shall keep the commandments of the LORD your God by walking in his ways and by fearing him.
ESV.7: For the LORD your God is bringing you into a good land, a land of brooks of water, of fountains and springs, flowing out in the valleys and hills,
ESV.8: a land of wheat and barley, of vines and fig trees and pomegranates, a land of olive trees and honey,
ESV.9: a land in which you will eat bread without scarcity, in which you will lack nothing, a land whose stones are iron, and out of whose hills you can dig copper.
ESV.10: And you shall eat and be full, and you shall bless the LORD your God for the good land he has given you.
ESV.11: “Take care lest you forget the LORD your God by not keeping his commandments and his rules and his statutes, which I command you today,
ESV.12: lest, when you have eaten and are full and have built good houses and live in them,
ESV.13: and when your herds and flocks multiply and your silver and gold is multiplied and all that you have is multiplied,
ESV.14: then your heart be lifted up, and you forget the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery,
ESV.15: who led you through the great and terrifying wilderness, with its fiery serpents and scorpions and thirsty ground where there was no water, who brought you water out of the flinty rock,
ESV.16: who fed you in the wilderness with manna that your fathers did not know, that he might humble you and test you, to do you good in the end.
ESV.17: Beware lest you say in your heart, ‘My power and the might of my hand have gotten me this wealth.’
ESV.18: You shall remember the LORD your God, for it is he who gives you power to get wealth, that he may confirm his covenant that he swore to your fathers, as it is this day.
ESV.19: And if you forget the LORD your God and go after other gods and serve them and worship them, I solemnly warn you today that you shall surely perish.
ESV.20: Like the nations that the LORD makes to perish before you, so shall you perish, because you would not obey the voice of the LORD your God.

NKJV.20: As the nations which the LORD destroys before you, so you shall perish, because you would not be obedient to the voice of the LORD your God.

NASB.3: 'He humbled you and let you be hungry, and fed you with manna which you did not know, nor did your fathers know, that He might make you understand that man does not live by bread alone, but man lives by everything that proceeds out of the mouth of the LORD.
NASB.4: 'Your clothing did not wear out on you, nor did your foot swell these forty years.
NASB.5: 'Thus you are to know in your heart that the LORD your God was disciplining you just as a man disciplines his son.
NASB.6: 'Therefore, you shall keep the commandments of the LORD your God, to walk in His ways and to fear Him.

NASB.8: a land of wheat and barley, of vines and fig trees and pomegranates, a land of olive oil and honey;
NASB.9: a land where you will eat food without scarcity, in which you will not lack anything; a land whose stones are iron, and out of whose hills you can dig copper.
NASB.10: 'When you have eaten and are satisfied, you shall bless the LORD your God for the good land which He has given you.
NASB.11: 'Beware that you do not forget the LORD your God by not keeping His commandments and His ordinances and His statutes which I am commanding you today;
NASB.12: otherwise, when you have eaten and are satisfied, and have built good houses and lived [in them],
NASB.13: and when your herds and your flocks multiply, and your silver and gold multiply, and all that you have multiplies,
NASB.14: then your heart will become proud and you will forget the LORD your God who brought you out from the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
NASB.15: 'He led you through the great and terrible wilderness, [with its] fiery serpents and scorpions and thirsty ground where there was no water; He brought water for you out of the rock of flint.
NASB.16: 'In the wilderness He fed you manna which your fathers did not know, that He might humble you and that He might test you, to do good for you in the end.

NASB.20: 'Like the nations that the LORD makes to perish before you, so you shall perish; because you would not listen to the voice of the LORD your God.

NLT.1: “Be careful to obey all the commands I am giving you today. Then you will live and multiply, and you will enter and occupy the land the LORD swore to give your ancestors.
NLT.2: Remember how the LORD your God led you through the wilderness for these forty years, humbling you and testing you to prove your character, and to find out whether or not you would obey his commands.
NLT.3: Yes, he humbled you by letting you go hungry and then feeding you with manna, a food previously unknown to you and your ancestors. He did it to teach you that people do not live by bread alone; rather, we live by every word that comes from the mouth of the LORD.
NLT.4: For all these forty years your clothes didn’t wear out, and your feet didn’t blister or swell.
NLT.5: Think about it: Just as a parent disciplines a child, the LORD your God disciplines you for your own good.
NLT.6: “So obey the commands of the LORD your God by walking in his ways and fearing him.
NLT.7: For the LORD your God is bringing you into a good land of flowing streams and pools of water, with fountains and springs that gush out in the valleys and hills.
NLT.8: It is a land of wheat and barley; of grapevines, fig trees, and pomegranates; of olive oil and honey.
NLT.9: It is a land where food is plentiful and nothing is lacking. It is a land where iron is as common as stone, and copper is abundant in the hills.
NLT.10: When you have eaten your fill, be sure to praise the LORD your God for the good land he has given you.
NLT.11: “But that is the time to be careful! Beware that in your plenty you do not forget the LORD your God and disobey his commands, regulations, and decrees that I am giving you today.
NLT.12: For when you have become full and prosperous and have built fine homes to live in,
NLT.13: and when your flocks and herds have become very large and your silver and gold have multiplied along with everything else, be careful!
NLT.14: Do not become proud at that time and forget the LORD your God, who rescued you from slavery in the land of Egypt.
NLT.15: Do not forget that he led you through the great and terrifying wilderness with its poisonous snakes and scorpions, where it was so hot and dry. He gave you water from the rock!
NLT.16: He fed you with manna in the wilderness, a food unknown to your ancestors. He did this to humble you and test you for your own good.
NLT.17: He did all this so you would never say to yourself, ‘I have achieved this wealth with my own strength and energy.’
NLT.18: Remember the LORD your God. He is the one who gives you power to be successful, in order to fulfill the covenant he confirmed to your ancestors with an oath.
NLT.19: “But I assure you of this: If you ever forget the LORD your God and follow other gods, worshiping and bowing down to them, you will certainly be destroyed.
NLT.20: Just as the LORD has destroyed other nations in your path, you also will be destroyed if you refuse to obey the LORD your God.

WEB.1: You shall observe to do all the commandments which I command you today, that you may live, and multiply, and go in and possess the land which Yahweh swore to your fathers.
WEB.2: You shall remember all the way which Yahweh your God has led you these forty years in the wilderness, that he might humble you, to prove you, to know what was in your heart, whether you would keep his commandments, or not.
WEB.3: He humbled you, and allowed you to be hungry, and fed you with manna, which you didn’t know, neither did your fathers know; that he might teach you that man does not live by bread only, but man lives by every word that proceeds out of Yahweh’s mouth.
WEB.4: Your clothing didn’t grow old on you, neither did your foot swell, these forty years.
WEB.5: You shall consider in your heart that as a man disciplines his son, so Yahweh your God disciplines you.
WEB.6: You shall keep the commandments of Yahweh your God, to walk in his ways, and to fear him.
WEB.7: For Yahweh your God brings you into a good land, a land of brooks of water, of springs, and underground water flowing into valleys and hills;
WEB.8: a land of wheat and barley, and vines and fig trees and pomegranates; a land of olive trees and honey;
WEB.9: a land in which you shall eat bread without scarceness, you shall not lack anything in it; a land whose stones are iron, and out of whose hills you may dig copper.
WEB.10: You shall eat and be full, and you shall bless Yahweh your God for the good land which he has given you.
WEB.11: Beware lest you forget Yahweh your God, in not keeping his commandments, and his ordinances, and his statutes, which I command you today;
WEB.12: lest, when you have eaten and are full, and have built fine houses, and lived in them;
WEB.13: and when your herds and your flocks multiply, and your silver and your gold is multiplied, and all that you have is multiplied;
WEB.14: then your heart might be lifted up, and you forget Yahweh your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage;
WEB.15: who led you through the great and terrible wilderness, with venomous snakes and scorpions, and thirsty ground where there was no water; who poured water for you out of the rock of flint;
WEB.16: who fed you in the wilderness with manna, which your fathers didn’t know; that he might humble you, and that he might prove you, to do you good at your latter end:
WEB.17: and lest you say in your heart, “My power and the might of my hand has gotten me this wealth.”
WEB.18: But you shall remember Yahweh your God, for it is he who gives you power to get wealth; that he may establish his covenant which he swore to your fathers, as it is today.
WEB.19: It shall be, if you shall forget Yahweh your God, and walk after other gods, and serve them, and worship them, I testify against you today that you shall surely perish.
WEB.20: As the nations that Yahweh makes to perish before you, so you shall perish; because you wouldn’t listen to Yahweh your God’s voice.

AMP.1: "Every commandment that I am commanding you today you shall be careful to do, so that you may live and multiply, and go in and possess the land which the LORD swore [to give] to your fathers.
AMP.2: And you shall remember [always] all the ways which the LORD your God has led you these forty years in the wilderness, so that He might humble you and test you, to know what was in your heart (mind), whether you would keep His commandments or not.
AMP.3: He humbled you and allowed you to be hungry and fed you with manna, [a substance] which you did not know, nor did your fathers know, so that He might make you understand [by personal experience] that man does not live by bread alone, but man lives by every word that proceeds out of the mouth of the LORD.
AMP.4: Your clothing did not wear out on you, nor did your feet swell these forty years.
AMP.5: Therefore, know in your heart (be fully cognizant) that the LORD your God disciplines and instructs you just as a man disciplines and instructs his son.
AMP.6: Therefore, you shall keep the commandments of the LORD your God, to walk [that is, to live each and every day] in His ways and fear [and worship] Him [with awe-filled reverence and profound respect].
AMP.7: For the LORD your God is bringing you into a good land, a land of brooks of water, of fountains and springs, flowing forth in valleys and hills;
AMP.8: a land of wheat and barley, and vines and fig trees and pomegranates, a land of olive oil and honey;
AMP.9: a land where you will eat bread without shortage, in which you will lack nothing; a land whose stones are iron, and out of whose hills you can dig copper.
AMP.10: When you have eaten and are satisfied, then you shall bless the LORD your God for the good land which He has given you.
AMP.11: "Beware that you do not forget the LORD your God by failing to keep His commandments and His judgments (precepts) and His statutes which I am commanding you today;
AMP.12: otherwise, when you have eaten and are satisfied, and have built good houses and lived in them,
AMP.13: and when your herds and flocks multiply, and your silver and gold multiply, and all that you have increases,
AMP.14: then your heart will become lifted up [by self-conceit and arrogance] and you will forget the LORD your God who brought you from the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
AMP.15: "He led you through the great and terrible wilderness, with its fiery serpents and scorpions and thirsty ground where there was no water; it was He who brought water for you out of the flinty rock.
AMP.16: "He fed you manna in the wilderness, [a substance] which your fathers did not know, so that He might humble you [by dependence on Him] and that He might test you, to do good [things] for you at the end.
AMP.17: Otherwise, you may say in your heart, 'My power and the strength of my hand made me this wealth.'
AMP.18: But you shall remember [with profound respect] the LORD your God, for it is He who is giving you power to make wealth, that He may confirm His covenant which He swore (solemnly promised) to your fathers, as it is this day.
AMP.19: And it shall come about if you ever forget the LORD your God and follow other gods and serve them and worship them, I testify against you today that you will most certainly perish.
AMP.20: Like the nations which the LORD causes to perish before you, so shall you perish; because you would not listen to and obey the voice of the LORD your God.

CSB17.1: “Carefully follow every command I am giving you today, so that you may live and increase, and may enter and take possession of the land <sup>ⓜ</sup> the LORD swore to your fathers.
CSB17.2: Remember that the LORD your God led you on the entire journey these forty years in the wilderness, so that he might humble you and test you to know what was in your heart, whether or not you would keep his commands.
CSB17.3: He humbled you by letting you go hungry; then he gave you manna to eat, which you and your fathers had not known, so that you might learn that man does not live on bread alone but on every word that comes from the mouth of the LORD. <sup>ⓝ</sup>
CSB17.4: Your clothing did not wear out, and your feet did not swell these forty years. <sup>ⓐ</sup>
CSB17.5: Keep in mind that the LORD your God has been disciplining you just as a man disciplines his son.
CSB17.6: So keep the commands of the LORD your God by walking in his ways and fearing him.
CSB17.7: For the LORD your God is bringing you into a good land, <sup>ⓑ</sup> a land with streams, springs, and deep water sources, flowing in both valleys and hills;
CSB17.8: a land of wheat, barley, vines, figs, and pomegranates; a land of olive oil and honey;
CSB17.9: a land where you will eat food without shortage, where you will lack nothing; a land whose rocks are iron and from whose hills you will mine copper.
CSB17.10: When you eat and are full, <sup>ⓒ</sup> you will bless the LORD your God for the good land <sup>ⓓ</sup> he has given you.
CSB17.11: “Be careful that you don’t forget the LORD your God by failing to keep his commands, ordinances, and statutes that I am giving you today.
CSB17.12: When you eat and are full, and build beautiful houses to live in,
CSB17.13: and your herds and flocks grow large, and your silver and gold multiply, and everything else you have increases,
CSB17.14: be careful that your heart doesn’t become proud and you forget the LORD your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the place of slavery. <sup>ⓔ</sup>
CSB17.15: He led you through the great and terrible wilderness with its poisonous <sup>[1]</sup> snakes and scorpions, a thirsty land where there was no water. He brought water out of the flint rock for you.
CSB17.16: He fed you in the wilderness with manna, <sup>ⓕ</sup> which your fathers had not known, in order to humble and test you, so that in the end he might cause you to prosper.
CSB17.17: You may say to yourself, ‘My power and my own ability have gained this wealth for me,’
CSB17.18: but remember that the LORD your God gives you the power to gain wealth, in order to confirm his covenant he swore to your fathers, <sup>ⓖ</sup> as it is today.
CSB17.19: If you ever forget the LORD your God and follow other gods to serve them and bow in worship to them, I testify against you today that you will perish. <sup>ⓗ</sup>

MSG.1: Keep and live out the entire commandment that I'm commanding you today so that you'll live and prosper and enter and own the land that God promised to your ancestors.
MSG.2: Remember every road that God led you on for those forty years in the wilderness, pushing you to your limits, testing you so that he would know what you were made of, whether you would keep his commandments or not.
MSG.3: He put you through hard times. He made you go hungry. Then he fed you with manna, something neither you nor your parents knew anything about, so you would learn that men and women don't live by bread only; we live by every word that comes from God's mouth.
MSG.4: Your clothes didn't wear out and your feet didn't blister those forty years.
MSG.5: You learned deep in your heart that God disciplines you in the same ways a father disciplines his child.
MSG.6: So it's paramount that you keep the commandments of God, your God, walk down the roads he shows you and reverently respect him.
MSG.7: God is about to bring you into a good land, a land with brooks and rivers, springs and lakes, streams out of the hills and through the valleys.
MSG.8: It's a land of wheat and barley, of vines and figs and pomegranates, of olives, oil, and honey.
MSG.9: It's land where you'll never go hungry—always food on the table and a roof over your head. It's a land where you'll get iron out of rocks and mine copper from the hills.
MSG.10: After a meal, satisfied, bless God, your God, for the good land he has given you.
MSG.11: Make sure you don't forget God, your God, by not keeping his commandments, his rules and regulations that I command you today
MSG.12: Make sure that when you eat and are satisfied, build pleasant houses and settle in,
MSG.13: see your herds and flocks flourish and more and more money come in, watch your standard of living going up and up—
MSG.14:
make sure you don't become so full of yourself and your things that you forget God, your God,
the God who delivered you from Egyptian slavery;
MSG.15:
the God who led you through that huge and fearsome wilderness, those desolate, arid badlands crawling with fiery snakes and scorpions;
the God who gave you water gushing from hard rock;
MSG.16: the God who gave you manna to eat in the wilderness, some-thing your ancestors had never heard of, in order to give you a taste of the hard life, to test you so that you would be prepared to live well in the days ahead of you.
MSG.17: If you start thinking to yourselves, "I did all this. And all by myself. I'm rich. It's all mine!"—
MSG.18: well, think again. Remember that God, your God, gave you the strength to produce all this wealth so as to confirm the covenant that he promised to your ancestors—as it is today.
MSG.19: If you forget, forget God, your God, and start taking up with other gods, serving and worshiping them, I'm on record right now as giving you firm warning: that will be the end of you; I mean it—destruction.
MSG.20: You'll go to your doom—the same as the nations God is destroying before you; doom because you wouldn't obey the Voice of God, your God.

NIV.1:
Do Not Forget the Lord
Be careful to follow every command I am giving you today, so that you may live and increase and may enter and possess the land that the Lord promised on oath to your forefathers.
NIV.2: Remember how the Lord your God led you all the way in the desert these forty years, to humble you and to test you in order to know what was in your heart, whether or not you would keep his commands.
NIV.3: He humbled you, causing you to hunger and then feeding you with manna, which neither you nor your fathers had known, to teach you that man does not live on bread alone but on every word that comes from the mouth of the Lord.
NIV.4: Your clothes did not wear out and your feet did not swell during these forty years.
NIV.5: Know then in your heart that as a man disciplines his son, so the Lord your God disciplines you.
NIV.6: Observe the commands of the Lord your God, walking in his ways and revering him.
NIV.7: For the Lord your God is bringing you into a good land—a land with streams and pools of water, with springs flowing in the valleys and hills;
NIV.8: a land with wheat and barley, vines and fig trees, pomegranates, olive oil and honey;
NIV.9: a land where bread will not be scarce and you will lack nothing; a land where the rocks are iron and you can dig copper out of the hills.
NIV.10: When you have eaten and are satisfied, praise the Lord your God for the good land he has given you.
NIV.11: Be careful that you do not forget the Lord your God, failing to observe his commands, his laws and his decrees that I am giving you this day.
NIV.12: Otherwise, when you eat and are satisfied, when you build fine houses and settle down,
NIV.13: and when your herds and flocks grow large and your silver and gold increase and all you have is multiplied,
NIV.14: then your heart will become proud and you will forget the Lord your God, who brought you out of Egypt, out of the land of slavery.
NIV.15: He led you through the vast and dreadful desert, that thirsty and waterless land, with its venomous snakes and scorpions. He brought you water out of hard rock.
NIV.16: He gave you manna to eat in the desert, something your fathers had never known, to humble and to test you so that in the end it might go well with you.
NIV.17: You may say to yourself, “My power and the strength of my hands have produced this wealth for me.”
NIV.18: But remember the Lord your God, for it is he who gives you the ability to produce wealth, and so confirms his covenant, which he swore to your forefathers, as it is today.
NIV.19: If you ever forget the Lord your God and follow other gods and worship and bow down to them, I testify against you today that you will surely be destroyed.
NIV.20: Like the nations the Lord destroyed before you, so you will be destroyed for not obeying the Lord your God.

NRSVCE.1: This entire commandment that I command you today you must diligently observe, so that you may live and increase, and go in and occupy the land that the LORD promised on oath to your ancestors.
NRSVCE.2: Remember the long way that the LORD your God has led you these forty years in the wilderness, in order to humble you, testing you to know what was in your heart, whether or not you would keep his commandments.
NRSVCE.3: He humbled you by letting you hunger, then by feeding you with manna, with which neither you nor your ancestors were acquainted, in order to make you understand that one does not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of the LORD.
NRSVCE.4: The clothes on your back did not wear out and your feet did not swell these forty years.
NRSVCE.5: Know then in your heart that as a parent disciplines a child so the LORD your God disciplines you.
NRSVCE.6: Therefore keep the commandments of the LORD your God, by walking in his ways and by fearing him.
NRSVCE.7: For the LORD your God is bringing you into a good land, a land with flowing streams, with springs and underground waters welling up in valleys and hills,
NRSVCE.8: a land of wheat and barley, of vines and fig trees and pomegranates, a land of olive trees and honey,
NRSVCE.9: a land where you may eat bread without scarcity, where you will lack nothing, a land whose stones are iron and from whose hills you may mine copper.
NRSVCE.10: You shall eat your fill and bless the LORD your God for the good land that he has given you.
NRSVCE.11: Take care that you do not forget the LORD your God, by failing to keep his commandments, his ordinances, and his statutes, which I am commanding you today.
NRSVCE.12: When you have eaten your fill and have built fine houses and live in them,
NRSVCE.13: and when your herds and flocks have multiplied, and your silver and gold is multiplied, and all that you have is multiplied,
NRSVCE.14: then do not exalt yourself, forgetting the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery,
NRSVCE.15: who led you through the great and terrible wilderness, an arid wasteland with poisonous snakes and scorpions. He made water flow for you from flint rock,
NRSVCE.16: and fed you in the wilderness with manna that your ancestors did not know, to humble you and to test you, and in the end to do you good.
NRSVCE.17: Do not say to yourself, “My power and the might of my own hand have gotten me this wealth.”
NRSVCE.18: But remember the LORD your God, for it is he who gives you power to get wealth, so that he may confirm his covenant that he swore to your ancestors, as he is doing today.
NRSVCE.19: If you do forget the LORD your God and follow other gods to serve and worship them, I solemnly warn you today that you shall surely perish.
NRSVCE.20: Like the nations that the LORD is destroying before you, so shall you perish, because you would not obey the voice of the LORD your God.

NET.1: You must keep carefully all these commandments I am giving you today so that you may live, increase in number, and go in and occupy the land that the LORD promised to your ancestors.
NET.2: Remember the whole way by which he has brought you these forty years through the desert so that he might, by humbling you, test you to see if you have it within you to keep his commandments or not.
NET.3: So he humbled you by making you hungry and then feeding you with unfamiliar manna. He did this to teach you that humankind cannot live by bread alone, but also by everything that comes from the LORD’s mouth.
NET.4: Your clothing did not wear out nor did your feet swell all these forty years.
NET.5: Be keenly aware that just as a parent disciplines his child, the LORD your God disciplines you.
NET.6: So you must keep his commandments, live according to his standards, and revere him.
NET.7: For the LORD your God is bringing you to a good land, a land of brooks, springs, and fountains flowing forth in valleys and hills,
NET.8: a land of wheat, barley, vines, fig trees, and pomegranates, of olive trees and honey,
NET.9: a land where you may eat food in plenty and find no lack of anything, a land whose stones are iron and from whose hills you can mine copper.
NET.10: You will eat your fill and then praise the LORD your God because of the good land he has given you.
NET.11: Be sure you do not forget the LORD your God by not keeping his commandments, ordinances, and statutes that I am giving you today.
NET.12: When you eat your fill, when you build and occupy good houses,
NET.13: when your cattle and flocks increase, when you have plenty of silver and gold, and when you have abundance of everything,
NET.14: be sure you do not feel self-important and forget the LORD your God who brought you from the land of Egypt, the place of slavery,
NET.15: and who brought you through the great, fearful desert of venomous serpents and scorpions, an arid place with no water. He made water flow from a flint rock and
NET.16: fed you in the desert with manna (which your ancestors had never before known) so that he might by humbling you test you and eventually bring good to you.
NET.17: Be careful not to say, “My own ability and skill have gotten me this wealth.”
NET.18: You must remember the LORD your God, for he is the one who gives ability to get wealth; if you do this he will confirm his covenant that he made by oath to your ancestors, even as he has to this day.
NET.19: Now if you forget the LORD your God at all and follow other gods, worshiping and prostrating yourselves before them, I testify to you today that you will surely be annihilated.
NET.20: Just like the nations the LORD is about to destroy from your sight, so he will do to you because you would not obey him.
